\chapter{Complexity — Counter Prog Poly Time}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.CounterProgPolyTime
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module shows that a counter program (a goto program over finitely many unary
natural-number registers that reads its input once and prints bits) which halts within
polynomially many abstract steps computes a polynomial-time computable function: its
compiled multi-tape Turing machine simulates $t$ abstract steps within $t(2t+3)$ machine
steps. This is how the emitters of [AB09, Remark~6.7] are shown to run in polynomial time.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time simulation of a counter program]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.polyTimeComputable}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.polyTimeComputable}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.exists_tm, Complexity.CounterProg.init, Complexity.CounterProg.run, Complexity.CounterProg.toTM, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a counter program with a finite label set $Lambda$ and decidable equality on
labels, and fix a start label $l_0\inLambda$. Let $f$ map binary strings to binary
strings, and let $C,c\inmathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every binary input $x$, there is a
time $t\le C(|x|+1)^c$ at which the run of $P$ from its initial state at $l_0$ has
halted and has output $f(x)$. Then $f$ is computable by a finite binary-alphabet Turing
machine in time $C' (n+1)^{c'}$ on every input of length $n$, for some natural numbers
$C',c'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-Time Computability from Bounded Runs]
\lean{Complexity.CounterProg.polyTimeComputable_of_goes}
\label{Complexity.CounterProg.polyTimeComputable_of_goes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CounterProg.Goes, Complexity.CounterProg.Instr, Complexity.CounterProg.init, Complexity.CounterProg.polyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable}
\difficulty{3}
Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda$ be a finite set of labels. Let $P$ be a counter
program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, let $\ell_0\in\Lambda$, and let $f$
map finite bit strings to finite bit strings. Suppose there are constants
$C,c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every input $x$ there are register values $\rho$ and a
read position $p$ for which, from the state with label $\ell_0$, all registers zero,
read position zero, and any previously printed output $o$, the program reaches the
halted state with registers $\rho$, read position $p$, and output $o$ followed by $f(x)$
in at most $C(|x|+1)^c$ steps. Then a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine computes $f$
in time bounded by a polynomial of the form $C'(|x|+1)^{c'}$ for some
$C',c'\in\mathbb{N}$ on every input.
\end{theorem}
